item.title: Hyakumangoku Matsuri: Kanazawa's Grand Samurai Procession Festival — Guide
item.description: Hyakumangoku Matsuri is Kanazawa’s largest annual festival, held each June to commemorate the 1583 entry of Maeda Toshiie into Kanazawa Castle, the event that established the powerful Maeda clan’s rule over the Kaga domain, whose rice yield of over a million koku gave the festival its name. The festival’s centrepiece is an elaborate procession of participants dressed in samurai-era costume re-enacting Toshiie’s triumphant entry, accompanied by traditional taiko drumming and dance performances, and the celebrations conclude with a lantern-lit boat parade along the Asano River.

item.title: Aoba Castle Ruins & the Date Masamune Festival — Guide
item.description: Perched on the wooded Aoba Hill above Sendai, the ruins of Aoba Castle — built by the one-eyed warlord Date Masamune in 1600 — command sweeping views over the city grid Masamune himself designed. A dramatic bronze equestrian statue of Masamune in full armour stands at the ruined honmaru, his crescent-moon helmet unmistakable against the sky. Each June, the Date Masamune Festival recreates his triumphant entry into Sendai with a horseback procession in full 17th-century armour.
